openQuestions.text: Which older Ponytail recommendations are already adopted, lost, or still new in current sk-code, and which source-inspired additions should be rejected?

resolvedQuestions.text: Which Ponytail teachings improve the four code-working agent definitions (.skilled/agents/code.md, review.md, debug.md, orchestrate.md) and their runtime mirrors, and which are already adopted there?
What is Ponytail 5.1.0 core doctrine, cost model, and smallest-complete-change ladder, and which parts are absent from the sk-code parent hub and its modes?

How do the hub `SKILL.md`, `ROUTER.md`, `hub-router.json` and `mode-registry.json` load the `sk-code/shared/` layer, and which shared files are loaded by nothing, loaded twice, or unreachable from any route?
Which original ideas does round three produce, which should be rejected with reasons, and what ranked findings table and implementation phases close the round?
How do Ponytail hooks activate, persist mode, track sessions, and gate behavior per runtime, and which mechanisms are missing from sk-code hooks?
Which Ponytail teachings improve the repository rules (.skilled/repo-rules/*.md) without weakening scope, evidence, verification or communication floors?
How do Ponytail commands and bundled skills delegate work, and how does that compare with sk-code mode-registry and hub-router routing?
Which Ponytail teachings improve the root REPO RULES.md and AGENTS.md framework, including the trigger-table load model?
How does stack detection behave for mixed stacks, monorepos and two-surface matches, and where do the surface packets' overrides of shared standards silently diverge?
Which Ponytail teachings improve the sk-code hub core (SKILL.md, ROUTER.md, mode-registry.json, hub-router.json) beyond what round one settled?
How does Ponytail stay portable across agent runtimes and rule-file copies, and which mechanisms could strengthen sk-code runtime surfaces and rule-copy checks?
How agnostic is `sk-code-review` as a mode meant for any codebase, and which repository-specific assumptions leak into its SKILL.md, references, assets, scripts and playbook?
Which Ponytail teachings improve the sk-code shared layer and the quality and review modes beyond round one's adopted set and defects?
What correctness, LOC-budget and quality enforcement does Ponytail ship, and what could sk-code-quality and sk-code-review adopt?
How does Ponytail measure its own effect, and what should sk-code benchmark harness adopt?
Which Ponytail teachings improve the per-surface packets (sk-code-webflow, sk-code-opencode, sk-code-obsidian, sk-code-quality) beyond round one's cited defects?
How do Ponytail's cross-runtime mirror and portability mechanics compare with the repo's generated mirrors and agent drift checks, and what should change?
Which ideas from the earlier 015 refinement are still adopted, which are missing after the two-axis hub rebuild, and which are LOST?
What do the review scripts do on foreign-repository inputs, and what would make the review logic stronger?
Which original ideas does Ponytail inspire for the agent definitions, repository rules and root docs, and which candidate transfers should be rejected with a reason?
Which Ponytail ideas should be rejected for sk-code and why, and what original ideas does Ponytail inspire that it does not contain?
Which round-two findings are NEW, ALREADY-COVERED or ALREADY-ADOPTED, and what priority does each carry for the ranked findings table?
What implementation phases should the refinement propose, gated on which risks?
Which Ponytail 5.1.0 mechanisms complement sk-code's current two-axis hub routing and shared prompt contracts without duplicating them?
Which Ponytail design restraint, quality, and review checks are genuinely missing from sk-code's nested code-quality and code-review modes?
Which Ponytail hook, state, and cross-runtime portability mechanisms can improve sk-code surfaces without violating its read-first, scope, and verification floors?
What do Ponytail's benchmark and correctness gates measure, and where could sk-code's benchmark and advisor tooling gain decision-useful evidence?

keyFindings.label: The reach list before editing is missing from @code's pre-implementation gate: Ponytail lists every place a change must reach (callers, tests, fixtures, config, exports) before writing, while @code's checklist checks scope, allowlist and routing but never enumerates the reach set. NEW target, ALREADY-COVERED idea (round one recommended it for workflow-implement.md).

keyFindings.text: The shared layer duplicates two of the Webflow packet's pattern assets with drifted content, and both copies are reachable from the routed map: shared/assets/patterns/{validation,wait}-patterns.js mirror sk-code-webflow/assets/patterns/ copies, both READMEs sit in the same IMPLEMENTATION row of RESOURCE_MAP, and the wait-patterns copies differ by a six-line cross-stack Motion reference present only in the Webflow copy while the shared copies carry an ASCII banner plus top-of-file 'use strict'. Reproducing case: diff shared/assets/patterns/wait-patterns.js sk-code-webflow/assets/patterns/wait-patterns.js prints the added Motion comment; rg for 'Cross-stack Motion reference' exits 1 in the shared copy and hits line 546 in the Webflow copy. NEW P1.

keyFindings.label: @code's RETURN contract has no gap-disclosure line: Ponytail ends every reply with what was skipped or not checked plus user risk, sk-code-review already adopted the analogous 'Not checked:' line, but @code's RETURN fields never name unchecked work or user-facing risk. NEW target, idea adopted on the review side.

@review has no no-case-no-finding evidence bar: Ponytail requires a concrete input or situation per finding before reporting, while @review's Issue Evidence Requirements ask only for file:line plus snippet or pattern reference and its adversarial pass challenges by disposition, not by demanding a case. NEW.

@review never reads the connected code as a named workflow step: Ponytail reads the diff then callers, called functions, tests and README, and greps every caller on signature or behavior change, while @review's ANALYZE step is tool-oriented and its Read-Budget Discipline discourages wide reads. The rules are compatible as coverage-once versus no-repeats. NEW.

keyFindings.text: Eight of the thirteen shared markdown files route readers through pre-merge directory families (references/webflow, references/opencode, references/motion_dev, assets/webflow, assets/universal) and none of those paths exists: the hub has no references/ dir, the only code-quality-checklist.md lives in sk-code-review/assets/, assets/universal/checklists/ is gone, and references/motion_dev/ is gone. 23 grep lines across 8 files, 22 of them path references in 7 files. Reproducing case: test -f on assets/webflow/checklists/code-quality-checklist.md fails while sk-code-review/assets/code-quality-checklist.md exists. NEW P1.

keyFindings.label: The ceiling: convention has no harvest report: Ponytail-debt scans markers into one debt ledger, flags no-trigger rows that silently rot, and closes with counts; sk-code has the producer convention and the reviewer downgrade rule but no reporting surface, so a marked deferral can become permanent unnoticed. NEW mechanism for sk-code-quality.

keyFindings.text: phase-detection.md is semantically stale beyond its dead paths: it says 'Both supported surfaces follow the same lifecycle' while the hub carries three surfaces, its per-phase tables list only WEBFLOW and OPENCODE, and its OPENCODE verification row names verify_alignment_drift.py alone while the live completion gate is the three-guard umbrella scripts/run-all-drift-guards.sh. Reproducing case: rg -n OBSIDIAN on phase-detection.md exits 1 while stack-detection.md counts several. NEW P1.

keyFindings.label: Round one's D2 (Codex-only changes passing unchecked) is closed in the current tree: the checker regex includes codex, its orphan list looks for .codex mirrors, both pre-commit hooks include codex paths, and the pre-commit mirror gate runs the dedicated Codex sync checks. VERIFIED CLOSURE; the parent should not reopen it as pending.

keyFindings.text: workflow-verify.md:86 carries a wrong validate.sh contract and contradicts the document that owns it: the shared file says warnings 'only become a failing validation outcome under --strict, which exits 2 unless the folder is grandfathered', while validation-rules.md:44 says 'a warning stays advice in both modes and never changes the exit code. A rule that should block reports an error itself', and :159 says only SPECKIT_COMPLETION_FRESHNESS_ENFORCE escalates a stale-freshness warn to an error that makes --strict exit 2. The authority states it owns this meaning and that copies elsewhere go stale first (validation-rules.md:835). Reproducing case: the two rg commands print claims that cannot both be true. NEW P1.

keyFindings.label: The Hermes agent-persona mirror check runs only in CI: sync-skills-hermes.cjs mirrors .skilled/agents personas into .hermes/skills/agent-* with a --check mode, CI runs both Hermes checks, but pre-commit has zero Hermes references and no .hermes entry in its mirror lists, the doctor runtime-mirror config has zero Hermes entries, and the doctor update route checks only Hermes prompts while the doctor doc claims agent mirrors too. NEW, same failure class as the closed D2.

keyFindings.text: The review mode's detect_surface_evidence misroutes generic repositories to the Webflow surface and contradicts the shared detection authority: any changed path containing package.json or src/ returns sk-code:code-webflow, while stack-detection.md:83 says generic Node.js without Webflow markers stays UNKNOWN and names the exact marker set (src/2_javascript/, *.webflow.js, Webflow.push, --vw-, vendor globals, wrangler.toml). Executed proof: text 'fix a null deref in the parser' with changed src/api/client.ts returns sk-code:code-webflow; 'review my dependency bump' with changed package.json returns sk-code:code-webflow. A generic-Node review therefore gets Webflow evidence and skips the unknown-disclosure path. NEW P1.

keyFindings.label: Restraint and simplification prompts have no front-door routing vocabulary: Ponytail activates on yagni, simplest solution, over-engineering and bloat, the sk-code hub owns the doctrine, but hub-router quality classes, mode-registry quality aliases, description.json keywords and ROUTER.md carry none of the vocabulary, so a simplify/over-engineered request cannot score the quality mode lexically. NEW.

keyFindings.text: The review mode has no Obsidian surface anywhere although the hub bundles Obsidian evidence into reviews: detect_surface_evidence has no OBSIDIAN branch, the output contract's surface-evidence line lists only two surfaces plus unknown, and review-core.md describes the field as code-webflow or code-opencode. A case-insensitive rg over SKILL.md, references/ and assets/ exits 1 outside the changelog. The hub's canary case surface-bundle-obsidian expects sk-code-review + sk-code-obsidian, and the shared precedence puts OBSIDIAN above WEBFLOW. Executed proof: 'code review my obsidian plugin' with changed main.ts returns sk-code:unknown. NEW P1.

keyFindings.label: Round one's doctrine-pass recommendation is fully implemented: the always-loaded ladder carries the reuse step as rung 2 of seven, its never-cut sentence names accessibility, the implement workflow carries the full reach list verbatim, and its Pre-Write Restraint repeats the ladder. VERIFIED CLOSURE; remaining reach-list gaps are only the outer layers.

Round one's review-output recommendation is fully implemented: Not checked with its exact placement, the performance workload inside Risk, the reworded consequence as User impact, and the widened removal search covering callers, tests, fixtures, config and string references. VERIFIED CLOSURE.

The review finding contract still lacks a reproducing case: Ponytail demands a concrete input or situation per finding, while the mode's format requires Risk, User impact, Finding class, Scope proof and Recommended fix, and its NEVER list bans vague findings without demanding reproducibility. NEW for the mode; the same gap was filed for @review in iteration 1.

The review mode's Phase 1 never enumerates the connected code: Ponytail reads callers of every changed function, the functions it calls, the tests and the README, while Phase 1 inspects the review target and loads standards and Phase 3 analyzes without a named read of callers or tests. NEW for the mode, ALREADY-COVERED idea at the agent layer.

D1 is fixed: the Webflow checker collects deferred callback errors from setTimeout and requestAnimationFrame through a run_callback wrapper and reports the first source and message, so a script whose deferred code throws now fails. VERIFIED CLOSURE.

D3 is fixed: the playbook index row points at the stack-folder validator scenario and the expected language list names all six folders (config, javascript, python, rust, shell, typescript). VERIFIED CLOSURE.

D4 is fixed: the shared stdin reader has a 3000 ms deadline that settles on stream end or deadline and clears timer and listeners, and both post-edit adapters import it instead of carrying their own copy. VERIFIED CLOSURE.

The precedence and Obsidian recommendation is closed across the surfaces: OBSIDIAN row and OPENCODE > OBSIDIAN > WEBFLOW > UNKNOWN in stack-detection, hub surface table and order, ROUTER.md vocabulary, playbook SD-004 with a dedicated scenario, both canary cases, and the advisor graph. VERIFIED CLOSURE.

Original idea: one authored agent source per dialect, generated elsewhere. Three byte-identical OpenCode-dialect copies exist with no equality check; declare .skilled/agents the authored source and generate .opencode/agents and .hermes/agents in the existing sync pipeline, as four other hosts already do.

Original idea: a vocabulary-parity check across the four routing surfaces (hub-router classes, mode-registry aliases, description keywords, canary corpus), modeled on the doctor's version parity: every alias asserted by the canary must resolve in the registries and every registry alias must be classifiable, failing with the missing surface named. Target: parent-skill-check or the compiled-routing gate.

keyFindings.text: The findings checker cannot see the finding shape its own doctrine prescribes, so that shape passes vacuously: review-core.md section 7 writes findings as headings with the number inside ('### 2 [P1] Missing authorization check') while check-review-findings.js matches only list items (/^(\d+)\. \S/). Observed: a faithful review-core-shaped review printed 'OK: no numbered findings to check' and exited 0, while the same review in the template list shape is checked line by line. The checker README's claim that it checks each numbered finding under ## Findings is false for one of the two shapes the packet documents. Reproducing case: run the checker on a review-core-shaped review. NEW P1.

keyFindings.label: Round-one closure ledger: recommendations 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and the D4 hook handoff are closed in the current tree; recommendation 2 is half closed (D1 fix landed, known-bad test input missing); recommendation 7 remains open; recommendation 10 stays deferred by design. VERIFIED.

Scope containment held for the whole run: every artifact written sits inside the lineage directory (ten narratives, nine deltas, nine record files, init event, config, strategy, gateway ledger and projection writes), no file outside was created or modified, and the only non-read commands were the append-gateway invocations whose writes land in the run directory. VERIFIED.

keyFindings.text: The quality mode, which owns the comment-hygiene gate, points operators at the legacy hooks and the shared universal standard repeats the same names: SKILL.md:130-131 names scripts/hooks/claude-posttooluse.sh as the write-time warning and .skilled/hooks/git/pre-commit as the commit block, and code-quality-standards.md:138-139 says the same, while the OpenCode naming file states the installed hook is .skilled/scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit (the core.hooksPath selection) and the live write-time adapter is .skilled/hooks/post-edit-quality/claude/claude-posttooluse.cjs, with the two older files kept as compatibility helpers for direct tests only. Both files exist, so a reader cannot tell which statement is current without a third document. Reproducing case: rg for both names across the three files prints two claims that cannot both be current. NEW P1.

shared/README.md still names the pre-rename packet keys (code-webflow, code-opencode, code-quality, code-review) and omits sk-code-obsidian, which now consumes the shared workflow trio through symlinks; the sentence is the index's only consumer list. Reproducing case: rg -n 'code-webflow|code-opencode|sk-code-obsidian' shared/README.md shows the stale names at line 17 and no obsidian mention. NEW P2.

Three overlapping exemption lists disagree about hub-level shared controls: ROUTER.md declares eight SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES as the exempt-from-leaf set, the router-sync guard keeps a nine-entry PARENT_TIER_ALLOWLIST that adds sk-code-review/assets/code-quality-checklist.md, and a third NON_ROUTED_ALLOWLIST also exempts references/stack-detection.md and references/phase-detection.md - two files loaded on every route via DEFAULT_RESOURCE, absent from leaf-manifest.json, yet never declared as shared controls. The hub's claim that 'the eight declared SHARED_CONTROL_RESOURCES are contained hub-level inputs' is narrower than the load contract it summarizes. NEW P2.

Verified as already adopted: all nine workflow-doctrine copies under sk-code-webflow, sk-code-opencode and sk-code-obsidian are symlinks into shared/references, so the single-source doctrine claim holds, and the hub version is parity-consistent across SKILL.md, mode-registry.json, description.json and hub-router.json at 2.2.4.0. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action; recorded so later iterations do not re-open it.

keyFindings.label: @review findings carry no assumed-load statement: Ponytail tells the reviewer to find the expected load and say which load was assumed, while @review's Performance dimension judges inefficiencies without naming the load. NEW target, ALREADY-COVERED idea (round one lodged the workload note for sk-code-review).

@review reports are not numbered across severity groups: Ponytail numbers findings across all groups so a user can say 'fix 2 and 5', while @review's report formats list P0, P1 and P2 sections with no shared numbering. NEW.

@review has no stated order of importance for report ordering: Ponytail fixes the order correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean, while @review carries rubric weights but no instruction to order the final report by them. NEW.

@code's bug-fix root-cause doctrine is already carried by the Critic pass: Ponytail's grep-every-caller and fix-root-cause-once rule is substantively adopted at code.md's wrong-abstraction Critic questions and SCOPE_CONFLICT escalation. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

@debug's response contract has no not-checked disclosure: Ponytail's audit ends with one line naming the parts not read or not runnable, while @debug's Success, Blocked and Escalation responses never name what could not be checked or run. NEW target, ALREADY-COVERED idea.

keyFindings.text: Cross-links inside the shared tier use three different forms for the same directory: stack-detection.md:154 links 'references/phase-detection.md' while its own sibling phase-detection.md links './stack-detection.md' correctly, and code-quality-standards.md:172 links bare 'references/universal/code-style-guide.md'. From stack-detection.md's directory the first link resolves to shared/references/references/phase-detection.md, which does not exist; no checker validates links inside referenced docs. Reproducing case: rg -n 'references/phase-detection.md' on stack-detection.md prints line 154. NEW P2.

keyFindings.label: @debug's fresh-observation and counter-evidence discipline is already adopted: Phase 1 demands an observation independent of prior attempts and Phase 4 searches counter-evidence and downgrades hypotheses, matching Ponytail's report-check discipline. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

keyFindings.text: Verified as already consistent: the precedence order OPENCODE > OBSIDIAN > WEBFLOW > UNKNOWN is identical in stack-detection.md:39, code-quality-standards.md:56 and hub SKILL.md:135; the AGENTS.md section 3 restraint-table pointer resolves (AGENTS.md:198); and the ceiling: harvest endpoint named by the style guide exists at sk-code-quality/scripts/ceiling-report.sh. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

keyFindings.label: Bounded candidates should disclose the omitted count: Ponytail caps audits at 20 findings and requires saying how many were left out, while @debug caps hypotheses at 2-3 without stating how many candidates were considered and dropped. NEW mechanism for debug.md Phase 3.

@orchestrate's sub-agent verification already covers Ponytail's report-check discipline: the mandatory review checklist verifies scope, file existence, evidence and hallucinated paths with named verification actions. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

The reach set is not a dispatch field in @orchestrate's Task Format: Ponytail's brief names callers, tests, fixtures, config and exports, while the Task Format carries Scope and Boundary but no reach-set field, though the orchestrator is who owns the reach set before the leaf starts. NEW target, ALREADY-COVERED idea.

@debug does not read the tests and build config covering the failing path: Ponytail's audit maps a repo by reading the README, deploy and build config, dependency list, entry points and tests first, while @debug Phase 2 traces call paths and checks recent changes but never reads the test harness or build config that exercise the failure. NEW for debug.md Phase 2.

keyFindings.text: The shared workflow trio and the repo rules carry the same floors twice with no pointer either way: reproduce/trace/one-cause in workflow-debug.md:50-57 vs root-cause-and-debugging.md:52-61; baseline/current/delta in workflow-verify.md:101-112 vs evidence-and-proof.md section 5; the mutation-check/negative-control ritual in workflow-verify.md:125-127 vs evidence-and-proof.md section 4; the pre-write restraint paragraph in workflow-implement.md:66 vs prevent-overengineering.md and AGENTS.md section 3. Every pair agrees in substance today, but the tiers load under different triggers, so a future edit can diverge unseen exactly as f-iter003-001 already did. Proposed repair: repo rules own the floors, shared files keep only the sk-code mechanism plus a one-line pointer. NEW P2.

The shared doctrine files carry surface-conditioned subsections while the hub's purity rule says shared material must never gain them: workflow-implement.md:78-84 and workflow-verify.md:76-99 embed 'OpenCode Surface Only' contracts (generate-context.js single-writer rule, sk-git boundary, validate.sh/tsc/rebuild-native chain) inside files symlinked into all three surfaces, while SKILL.md:163 says shared backend material 'must never gain per-mode workflow contracts' and sk-code-opencode already owns a shared tier (references/shared/alignment-verification-automation.md) where they can live. Reproducing case: rg -n 'OpenCode Surface Only' on the shared references prints four hits. NEW P2.

keyFindings.label: The OpenCode-dialect agent body exists in three byte-identical copies (.skilled/agents, .opencode/agents, .hermes/agents) with no equality check between them: each checker compares a different pair, the doctor roster check treats .skilled as presence-only, and the Hermes and Pi syncs source from .skilled, so an edit that satisfies one pair checker can leave the other copies stale with every local gate green. NEW, latent.

Ponytail's adapter-thinness rule is substantively implemented: Cursor agents are symlinks resolving to the Claude canonical, Devin and Codex trees are generated, and the runtime-mirrors policy documents which dialect each host parses. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

keyFindings.text: Verified as already consistent: the seven-rung ladder summary in workflow-implement.md:66 matches code-quality-standards.md:46-52 rung for rung including the reuse rung and the never-cut tail, and every repo-rule pair in f-iter003-002 agrees in substance today (reproduce, trace, one cause, whole-gate re-run, baseline, negative control). ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action beyond the pointer proposal.

keyFindings.label: The reach set is only half-enumerated in the pre-write pass: Ponytail lists callers, tests, fixtures, config and exports, while prevent-overengineering.md Sec2 asks for the owning module, one real caller and the contract (the dangerous half) but not the rest. ALREADY-COVERED idea, NEW target.

keyFindings.text: The OpenCode surface enforces a comment budget the shared universal tier does not have and nothing measures: 'Maximum 3 comments per 10 lines of code' appears in naming-and-commenting.md:170 and in every language style guide and five checklists (14 rows across 13 files), while the shared universal guide defaults to no comments and requires one only for hidden constraints and invariants with no quantity rule, and no checker counts comments. A 10-line security block with four durable WHY comments violates the checklist row and satisfies the universal contract. Reproducing case: rg -n '3 comments per 10|max 3 comments per 10' .skilled/skills/sk-code --glob '!benchmark/**' prints 14 rows across 13 files; rg over sk-code-quality/scripts finds no count-enforcing script. NEW P2.

A live OpenCode reference carries a packet-number pointer in its own prose: naming-and-commenting.md:283 reads 'Carry-over from 139: keep rule constants centralized...' while the same file's section 4 declares ephemeral-artifact pointers forbidden and calls the rule a HARD BLOCK. The pointer sits in documentation, not a code comment, so no hook scans it, but it is the dangling-reference class the rule exists to stop. Reproducing case: rg -n 'Carry-over from' .skilled/skills/sk-code --glob '!benchmark/**' prints this one row and no other. NEW P2.

keyFindings.label: The decodability floor for minimal diffs is absent: Ponytail says a one-liner that needs decoding is not short, while the repo settles size purely by reversal cost with no counterweight against unreadable golf. NEW for prevent-overengineering.md Sec1.

keyFindings.text: The mode registry's own description omits the third surface it registers: mode-registry.json:5 describes the surface axis as '(sk-code-webflow/sk-code-opencode)' while extensions.surface-axis.surfaces:19 lists sk-code-obsidian and the modes array carries its full entry at 98-110. The same stale two-surface phrasing recurs in shared/README.md:17. Reproducing case: rg -n 'sk-code-webflow/sk-code-opencode' mode-registry.json prints line 5. NEW P2.

keyFindings.label: Moved or merged code is not required to keep its error handling and validation: Ponytail states the rule, while the rules only forbid deliberately cutting error handling and treat rename/move as mechanical in-scope changes. NEW for scope-discipline.md Sec2 or prevent-overengineering.md Sec5.

keyFindings.text: No test covers an OBSIDIAN-versus-WEBFLOW collision, the one precedence decision that needs it: stack-detection.md section 4 has Webflow, Obsidian, and mixed-.skilled/ rows but none where a target set satisfies both Obsidian repo-root markers and a Webflow marker, and the canary corpus's eleven cases include no collision case. A wrong order would silently route Obsidian plugin work through Webflow standards or the reverse. Reproducing case: the fixture's cases[].id list has surface-bundle-reference, surface-bundle-obsidian, single-webflow, single-obsidian and no collision case; stack-detection.md's section 4 table carries no combined row. NEW P2.

keyFindings.label: No tiebreaker for equal-cost options on edge-case correctness: Ponytail takes the option correct on edge cases when sizes tie, while the reversal-cost order breaks ties by cost only. NEW for prevent-overengineering.md Sec1.

Accessibility is absent from the rules never-cut set: Ponytail names it, the rules carry the request, error-handling and dependency floors, and the word appears in none of the 14 rule files. ALREADY-COVERED idea (round one), NEW target for the rules.

keyFindings.text: A Webflow enforcement file keeps a stale link label while pointing at the right target: enforcement.md:310 renders a link whose label text is '../../../assets/webflow/checklists/code-quality-checklist.md' and whose target is '../../../sk-code-quality/assets/code-quality-checklist/overview-header-and-comments.md'. The target resolves, but a reader who copies the label lands on a missing file. Reproducing case: test -f .skilled/skills/sk-code/assets/webflow/checklists/code-quality-checklist.md returns no while the link target exists. NEW P2.

keyFindings.label: The root-cause doctrine already beats Ponytail's version: reproduce the exact symptom, locate the producer, trace its other consumers, fix at the source and re-run the failing check plus the whole gate. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

Ponytail's closing gap-disclosure line is already required in stronger form: evidence-and-proof.md Sec10 requires a four-part close-out plus an explicit what-is-not-done statement, which sharpens the @code RETURN gap finding. ALREADY-ADOPTED at the rules layer.

The close-out contract never discloses a residual risk: Ponytail closes with what was skipped or not checked plus any risk the user must know, while the repo close-out lists what ran, what is inferred, what only the operator can verify and what is not done, and the word risk never appears in evidence-and-proof.md or communication-handoff.md. NEW for AGENTS.md Sec10 and evidence-and-proof.md Sec10.

keyFindings.text: The two surfaces cap comment quantity at different numbers and the universal contract has none: Webflow says 'Maximum 5 comments per 10 lines of code' (cross-language-rules.md:47, repeated in javascript/quick-reference.md:68) while OpenCode says three (naming-and-commenting.md:170 plus twelve more files), and the universal guide defines comment policy by purpose with no count. Both thresholds are surface rules over the same shared contract and neither cites a surface reason, so the same file shape is judged differently depending on route. Reproducing case: rg -n 'comments per 10' .skilled/skills/sk-code prints the Webflow rows at 5 and the OpenCode rows at 3 in one output. NEW P2.

The relative link labels in surface shared-tier files are stale pre-move paths even where targets resolve: cross-language-rules.md:173 labels a link '../../universal/code-style-guide.md' over target '../../../shared/references/universal/code-style-guide.md', and the OpenCode naming file does the same over a four-level target at line 235. With enforcement.md:310 (iteration 4) the label-drift class now has four instances across three files, enough for one sweep rather than four fixes. Reproducing case: rg -n '\[../../universal/code-style-guide' .skilled/skills/sk-code prints both labels; neither label path exists from the containing file's directory. NEW P2.

keyFindings.label: Accessibility is absent from the root framework and the never-cut floor is split: Ponytail keeps one never-cut list including accessibility, while the root docs carry no list at all and the word accessibility appears in neither AGENTS.md nor REPO RULES.md. ALREADY-COVERED idea (round one), NEW target.

keyFindings.text: Verified single-sourced and non-contradicting: the two structure rules (no double-underscore folder names, tests under a tests/ tree) appear only in the universal guide and have no surface copies to drift; the OpenCode surface's P0 restatements (boundary validation, secrets) add language examples while agreeing with the universal P0 list.
